entries.repro: 'research KPIT Technologies' (ollama, normal) -> chat: 'dividend yield of 0.0142%' and 'market cap of ₹1.44 lakh crores' while the brief panel (replay) shows 'Dividend yield 1.42%' and 'INR 144.02B' (screener.in 2026-09-23: yield 1.42%, mcap ₹14,504 cr); COCHINSHIP turn 1: 'revenue growth of 0.024%, earnings growth of -0.193%' (true 2.4% / -19.3%)

Correction: the market-cap half is a different mechanism — market_cap reaches the model as a raw rupee number (144021815296.0) with no mislabelled unit, and the model mis-converted it (₹1.44 lakh crore vs the true ~₹14,402 crore, 10x); the fix shape (pre-scaled, unit-spelled crore) still applies. Severity unchanged: wrong money figures stated as true in the primary chat surface.
entries.root_cause: semantics.py emits fraction-valued metrics (growth, promoter/institutional share, dividend yield) with unit 'percent'; the brief panel's formatDerived multiplies 'percent' by 100 so the panel is right, but the model receives the raw bundle and reads 0.0142 'percent' as 0.0142%. Market cap reaches the model as a raw rupee float with no scaled unit and the model mis-converts it (10x).
entries.fix_shape: Make the unit honest by construction: emit unit 'fraction' (or pre-scale to percent points) for every fraction metric and give money in crore with the unit spelled out; one shared formatter feeds both panel and tool payload. Pin with a test asserting every semantics metric whose unit is 'percent' has value in percent points, plus a KPIT/COCHINSHIP fixture that checks the tool payload a model reads.

entries.root_cause: _dispatch_tool_with_progress starts the tool with asyncio.create_task; its finally only resets the step sink and never cancels the task, and `await task` is reached only on the happy path, so a generator close (client disconnect / Stop) orphans the task.
entries.fix_shape: In the generator's finally: if not task.done(): task.cancel(); await it under suppress(CancelledError); make research engines cancellation-clean. Test: aclose() the dispatch generator mid-tool and assert the tool task is cancelled (not finished) within 100 ms.

entries.title: Gemini thought signatures are dropped on multi-round tool turns: the adapter keeps only name/args and rebuilds function_call parts without the signature Google documents as required for Gemini 3 function calling
entries.repro: design (code read) + NOT TESTED live. GeminiProvider.stream_chat reads only fc.name / fc.id / fc.args from each part (the Part's thought_signature field, present in google-genai 2.5.0, `'thought_signature' in types.Part.model_fields` -> True, is never read). LLMToolUseEvent has no slot to carry it. _split_system_and_contents rebuilds the model turn as {'function_call': {name, args}} parts. Round 2 of any Gemini 3 tool turn therefore replays function calls without their signatures. Live confirmation needs a Gemini key (none funded on this run's lanes). Cost: one 2-round agent invoke on a Gemini 3 Flash-class model, < $0.01.

We recommend you always pass all signatures back as received, but it's *required* for function calling signatures.'; line 649: 'Return the entire response with all parts back to the model in subsequent turns.'; line 651: 'Don't merge one part with a signature with another part without a signature.'); https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-3.md.txt (line 226: 'If you are managing conversation history manually, you must include thought blocks with their signatures in subsequent requests to validate authenticity.')
entries.root_cause: LLMToolUseEvent has no slot for provider metadata, gemini.py:155-163 reads only name/id/args, and _split_system_and_contents rebuilds function_call parts from name+args, so part.thought_signature is always lost between rounds.
entries.fix_shape: Add optional provider_meta to LLMToolUseEvent, capture thought_signature (base64 in transit), carry it in metadata['tool_calls'][i] and re-attach it to the matching function_call part. Wire-shape replay test per the eval-loop entry. Needs one live Gemini 3 check.

entries.title: Research LLM calls are unmeterable: the research BudgetGuard never sets token/spend ceilings and every record() passes usage=None, so cost ceilings can never fire and every brief reports $0 / 0 tokens
entries.repro: Run any native research brief. LLMCall is typed Callable[[list[dict]], Awaitable[str]] (deep.py:54) - there is no channel for usage - so every budget call site passes None: citecheck.py:266, deep.py:1214, iter.py:585, iter.py:962, iter.py:1023, verify.py:319. BudgetGuard.record returns immediately after ticking _steps when usage is None (budget_guard.py:126-127), so _tokens and _spend_usd stay 0 for the whole run. breach() checks tokens then spend first (budget_guard.py:152-158) and neither can ever trip. BudgetGuard.cost() therefore returns {'tokens': 0, 'spend_usd': 0.0, 'steps': n} -> ResearchBrief.cost (models.py:168) -> formatBriefTokens(0) and formatBriefSpend(0) both return null (brief-ingest.ts:445, brief-ingest.ts:459) -> the cockpit shows NO cost for a native deep run while the Sonar lane shows '~$0.25 (estimate)' (sonar.py:224-238).

The research llm_call wraps oneshot.complete, which returns only a str (deep_research.py:322-325, oneshot.py:46-53), so every research record() call passes None and cost() reports tokens 0 / spend 0.0, which the cockpit then omits. entries.root_cause: LLMCall is typed Callable[[list[dict]], Awaitable[str]], wrapping oneshot.complete which returns only text, so there is no usage channel; deep_research builds the guard with only max_steps/max_wall_seconds; a zero meaning 'unmeasured' renders as 'free'.
entries.fix_shape: Return (text, usage) from oneshot.complete and thread usage through LLMCall into BudgetGuard.record; set token/spend ceilings on the research guard; render unmeasured cost as unknown, never 0. entries.title: Workflow runs carry no BYOK credentials, and the resulting LLM failure is recorded as a successful node whose output is '(no provider key configured)'

BudgetConfig.tsx:40-45: e.target.value === '' -> n = undefined -> Number.isFinite(undefined) is false -> maxSpendUsd: undefined. lib/delegate-runs.ts:97-102 puts it in the body and JSON.stringify DROPS the key, so the sidecar receives no max_spend_usd; sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:152-156 guards every ceiling behind `if self.max_X is not None`, so absent = no ceiling. The durable background run has unlimited spend. || [COD-runs-durable-delegate-12] In the Delegate budget editor clear the 'sec' field -> onChange stores undefined -> JSON omits it -> max_wall_seconds=None -> asyncio.timeout(None) is a no-op; a stalled provider stream then holds the run in `running` forever. Clear all four -> only _MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS bounds the run. 0 / negative values are accepted and abort instantly.
entries.evidence: src/modules/chat/BudgetConfig.tsx:5-13, src/modules/chat/BudgetConfig.tsx:28-46, src/lib/delegate-runs.ts:96-103, sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:96-106, sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:152-157, sidecar/models/run.py:53-59 and :91 (all ceilings Optional, default None, no gt=0), sidecar/services/run_manager.py:258 (`budget or RunBudget()`), :145-152 (comment: 'the LLM adapters carry no per-stream timeout'; timeout(None) no-op), sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:3-4 ('unsafe to ship without a spend ceiling'), src/modules/chat/BudgetConfig.tsx:41-44 (empty input -> undefined) || refuter corrections: COD-frontend-panels-agent-shell-7: Mechanism confirmed: clearing a budget box sets that key to undefined, JSON.stringify drops it, RunBudget defaults it to None (models/run.py:55), and BudgetGuard.breach skips None ceilings, with no server-side default. Corrected: clearing only the '$' box does not make the run unbounded, because the token (120k), wall-clock (600 s) and step (12) ceilings still abort it. Truly unbounded spend needs all four boxes cleared, which is a deliberate multi-step act. Still a real hole in a component that promises 'never unbounded', so medium, not high.
entries.root_cause: BudgetConfig maps an empty box to undefined, JSON drops it, RunBudget ceilings are Optional with no default or gt=0, BudgetGuard skips None ceilings and asyncio.timeout(None) is a no-op; the trust gate depends on the client remembering to send it.
entries.fix_shape: Server-side floor in launch_run: fill each None ceiling from DEFAULT_BUDGET and add Field(gt=0); client falls back to the default on an empty box. Test: POST a run with an empty budget -> guard carries all four defaults.

entries.title: Resume/answer re-enter a Delegate run with provider, model and api_key all None, so the 'resumable checkpoint' cannot work for any BYOK cloud run (and no UI calls resume)
entries.repro: Launch with provider=openrouter + key, let it breach (status=error), POST /runs/{id}/resume -> invoke_agent is called with provider/model/api_key all None (proved: scratch script prints `P4 resume invoke kwargs: {'provider': None, 'model': None, 'api_key': None}`), so it falls to spec.default_provider ('anthropic' for 10 bundled agents, keyless -> error; 'ollama' -> cold-loads a local model).

Severity lowered high->medium because no UI path reaches either resume (resumeDelegateRun has zero callers) or answer (no pause trigger, finding 10), so no user hits the failure today - it is a dead/false SC-008 claim rather than a broken core flow.
entries.root_cause: provider/model were never persisted with the run and the resume/answer routes accept no key; cost is also reset to RunCost() on resume.
entries.fix_shape: Persist provider+model in _PERSISTED_OPTION_KEYS, accept apiKey (header) on resume/answer, accumulate cost across resumes, and add a Resume control. Test: resume invokes with the persisted provider/model and the passed key.

entries.title: Resume and answer corrupt a Delegate conversation: the original prompt is replayed as the newest turn after the human's answer, and a second answer turns the first answer into the prompt
entries.repro: launch('ORIGINAL PROMPT') -> pause -> answer('ANSWER ONE'): provider receives [assistant, user 'ANSWER ONE', user 'ORIGINAL PROMPT']. pause -> answer('ANSWER TWO'): provider receives [..., user 'ORIGINAL PROMPT', assistant, user 'ANSWER TWO', user 'ANSWER ONE'] - the prompt is now the first answer (scratch proof P1a/P1b).
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/run_manager.py:126-129 (_drive_run writes history first, then the prompt, so the checkpoint no longer starts with the prompt), :369-382 (resume assumes 'first user turn = prompt'), :338-343 (answer appended as a raw dict), sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:518-520 (history, then prompt as the last message), sidecar/services/run_manager.py:164-173 (tool RESULTS are never checkpointed, so a resumed run re-pays every tool call), sidecar/services/runs_store.py:27-28 (column documented as 'the accumulated messages list' - it is a display digest)
entries.root_cause: _drive_run writes history then the prompt, while resume_run assumes the first user turn is the prompt; the checkpoint format is known to four places with its one invariant broken by its own writer.
entries.fix_shape: Store {prompt, turns[]} explicitly; on answer send the answer as the new prompt with prior turns as history. Test: launch -> answer -> answer produces the correct provider message order.

entries.title: The Delegate spend/token ceiling can overshoot: a breach flagged at a round boundary cannot stop the loop, so that round's tools run and the next provider request is sent and never metered
entries.repro: Faked provider that emits tool_use + done(100k tokens) every round, RunBudget(max_tokens=1000): the run aborts with 'token ceiling' but the provider was called TWICE (scratch proof prints `P5 ... provider calls after 1-round breach: 2 | cost: tokens=100000`) - round 2's request went out after the breach and its usage is not in the recorded cost.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/run_manager.py:133-140 (callback only sets a flag), sidecar/services/run_manager.py:176-178 (the consumer can act only on the NEXT yielded event), sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1466-1473 (callback fires, then `break` to tool dispatch), sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1551-1575 (all pending tools dispatched - incl. paid search / deep research - before any event is guaranteed), sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:1-8 ('hard spend ceiling', 'aborts 100%')
entries.root_cause: _on_round_usage only sets a flag; invoke_agent breaks to tool dispatch without yielding, so the consumer can stop only on the next yielded event.
entries.fix_shape: Let the callback stop the loop (return a stop bool that invoke_agent honours before dispatch, or raise a private _BudgetBreach). Test: max_tokens=1000 with a 100k-token round -> exactly one provider call.

entries.title: A Delegate run that completes on the round that touches a ceiling is recorded as error, hiding a finished answer
entries.repro: One-shot provider (delta + done), RunBudget(max_steps=1) -> row is status=error, detail='step ceiling 1 reached (1 taken)' while its transcript holds the complete answer (scratch proof P2). Same for a final round that crosses max_tokens / max_spend_usd.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:162 (`>=` on an integer count: a budget of N steps aborts ON the Nth), sidecar/services/run_manager.py:183-188 (breach_reason wins even when the generator finished naturally), sidecar/services/run_manager.py:175 (`breach_reason` also carries agent error text - one variable, two meanings)
entries.root_cause: breach() uses >= on the step count and breach_reason wins over natural completion; breach_reason also carries agent error text.
entries.fix_shape: Record whether the final terminator was seen and prefer status=done with the ceiling noted; use > for steps. Test: one-shot provider with max_steps=1 ends done.

entries.repro: design, verified in code: agent proposes portfolio_delete_position for a hand-entered holding (or write_note mode=replace on a symbol note) -> user clicks Accept (or AUTO applies it with no click, proposed-changes.ts:118-120) -> apply removes the holding / overwrites the note (host-actions.ts:1376-1389, 1176-1192) -> the change leaves ProposedChangesReview, which renders only status==='pending' (ProposedChangesReview.tsx:27) -> no Undo, no restorable pre-image (the stored 'before' is a prose string, host-actions.ts:790-815), no note/portfolio version history (src/store/notes.ts, src/store/portfolios.ts). entries.title: Tool-call ids are not unique (Ollama '' for every call, Gemini name_index reset per round, rescued leaks 'leaked-0', auto-briefs '__autobrief'), so on the default local lane no host action can be acked and applied changes are narrated as 'pending', while a stale ack falsely confirms later briefs for 10 minutes
entries.repro: (a) Ollama (the store's defaultProviderId): SDK ToolCall has no id field, adapter emits tool_call_id='' -> frontend ackHostAction returns early on an empty id and ActionAckRequest requires min_length=1 -> every AUTO host action (set_chart_symbol, open_panel, write_note...) is rewritten to status 'dispatched_unconfirmed' ('do not report it as done') after a 0.8 s grace wait, every round. (b) Gemini: round 1 set_chart_symbol gets id 'set_chart_symbol_0', panel acks 'applied'; round 2 (or any run within the 600 s TTL) issues set_chart_symbol again -> same id -> _await_host_action_acks finds the stale entry immediately and the model is told the NEW action 'applied' before the panel has processed it (or even if it later keeps_previous). || [SURF-COMPOSER-CHAT-8] any auto host action on ollama (12-multiturn-t3-watchlist add_to_watchlist x2, 16-multiturn-t6-arrange arrange_layout) -> tool_use.tool_call_id is '' -> ackHostAction returns early -> runtime result 'dispatched_unconfirmed' -> model: '… pending confirmation' for a change that was applied (replay label 'Added … to your watchlist') || [SURF-RESEARCH-BRIEFS-9] Every llama3.1:8b tool_use this session streamed tool_call_id '' (r2-deep-cgpower 12 events, r3-ultra-kaynes 28, r5 2, conv1-t1 2, conv1-t2 1). The frontend's ack for such a call is skipped (`if (!toolCallId) return`), and even a direct POST /agents/actions/ack {tool_call_id:'', status:'applied'} -> HTTP 422 'String should have at least 1 character'. So under autonomy=auto the runtime's grace-window read-back always finds no entry. || [SURF-RESEARCH-BRIEFS-12] same sidecar (pid 15507): turn 1 auto-publish acked applied as '__autobrief' at 08:06:03; turn 2 'research Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders' (ollama, auto) with NO ack from any client -> publish_brief '__autobrief' at 08:12:02, zero 'did not confirm the publish' notices, model says 'Built a brief on Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders.'; control on a fresh process with no prior ack (run 30) -> the notice fires (1) || [COD-llm-adapters-11] DeepSeek/OpenRouter/Ollama round 1 leaks a tool call as text with no id -> rescued as tool_call_id='leaked-0'; round 3 leaks another -> also 'leaked-0'. entries.root_cause: Uniqueness of tool_call_id is an unstated invariant every consumer relies on (tool pairing, the process-global ack ledger, publish_brief read-back) but no layer enforces it: the Ollama SDK has no id field, Gemini mints f'{name}_{index}' per stream, the leak rescue hardcodes 'leaked-0', and the auto-publish id derives from the empty provider id; the ledger never pops an ack.
entries.fix_shape: The runtime mints a uuid tool_call_id whenever the provider's is empty or already seen in the conversation (one place), the auto-publish id uses a uuid/run id, and action_ledger.get pops. entries.title: No prompt caching on the Anthropic lane, and the per-turn terminal preamble is folded into the one system string, so every round re-bills ~11.5k tokens of schemas and prompt at full price
entries.repro: design: any Anthropic BYOK turn (the default provider of 11 of the 13 first-party agents — every persona plus portfolio_advisor and strategy_critic). The adapter sends tools + one concatenated system string + messages with no cache_control breakpoint; a 4-round tool turn sends the ~11.5k-token prefix 5 times uncached. Even with a breakpoint, the system string changes every turn because the terminal preamble (focused chart, watchlist, open panels, viewport) is joined into it.

entries.title: run_custom_backtest advertises readOnlyHint=true on the external MCP surface while it writes to the in-process backtest result cache
entries.repro: External MCP client lists tools -> run_custom_backtest carries annotations.readOnlyHint=true -> client auto-approves it as a read -> the call persists a BacktestResult into the shared backtest_store. Declared safety hint is false.

entries.title: Ollama silently retries a round without tools on a client-side tools-construction error, with no log or event
entries.repro: Ollama daemon returns a transient 500 (or any error) on the tools-enabled chat call -> adapter swallows the exception with no log, reopens the stream WITHOUT tools, and the model answers from training data instead of calling get_quote; the stream looks completely normal to the user
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/llm/ollama.py:139-149, sidecar/services/llm/ollama.py:150-169 || refuter corrections: COD-llm-adapters-2: The repro mechanism is wrong: ollama.AsyncClient.chat(stream=True) returns a lazy async generator and makes no HTTP request at await time, so a 500/connection error/'model does not support tools' surfaces during iteration and is humanized into an LLMErrorEvent (ollama.py:228-237), never a silent tool-less retry. The bare `except Exception: stream = None` (no log) only catches client-side construction errors (e.g. a Tool.model_validate failure on a malformed schema); a TypeError from an unknown kwarg recurs on the retry and surfaces as an error. Residual: a swallowed, unlogged exception, and the retry-without-tools fallback is effectively dead for its documented purpose. high -> low.

entries.fix_shape: Narrow the except to the specific validation error and log + emit a notice when tools are dropped. Test: a Tool.model_validate failure logs and yields a notice.

entries.title: The backtest DSL folds case for fields and functions but not keywords: 'SMA(20) > 50 AND close > 1' fails at AND
entries.repro: sidecar/.venv/bin/python -c: compile_rule('SMA(20) > 50 AND close > 1') -> DslError "unexpected 'AND'" at the AND's column, while compile_rule('SMA(20) > 50 and close > 1') parses. The editor shows a caret under a token the user just watched work in uppercase two words earlier.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/backtest_dsl.py:346 (`name = token.text.lower()` — fields and functions are case-insensitive), sidecar/services/backtest_dsl.py:237 (`token.text == word` — keywords are case-sensitive), src/modules/backtest/custom-strategy-editor.tsx:76-94 (renders the positioned error)
entries.root_cause: _accept_keyword compares token.text == word case-sensitively while _primary lowercases identifiers.
entries.fix_shape: Compare token.text.lower() in _accept_keyword. Test: uppercase AND/OR parse.
